items.title: Welcome to OpenStudio Hub
items.text:
The zero-trust, automated pipeline orchestrator for modern 3D studios.

OpenStudio Hub is an advanced Desktop Client designed to eliminate daily production friction. By bridging the gap between your project management (Kitsu/Gazu), your version control system (SVN/Git), and your 3D Digital Content Creation tools (Blender), it ensures a bulletproof Golden Path for your artists.

Say goodbye to missing textures, broken scene scales, and misnamed folders.

items.title: 🚀 Why OpenStudio Hub?
items.text:
We built this tool to solve the most expensive problem in 3D production: Human Error.

  • Automated QA & Auto-Fixing (Gatekeeper): Detects and automatically fixes missing textures, dirty geometry, and wrong naming conventions before the artist publishes their work.
  • Vendor Jailing & Sparse Checkout: Protects your IP and saves bandwidth. Freelancers only download the exact files they need for their assigned task, nothing else.
  • Automated Task Orchestration: Connects directly to Kitsu. Translates database tasks into physical folder structures and generates master .blend files automatically.
  • Standardized Workspaces: Downloads exact Blender versions and extensions, running them in an isolated sandbox to ensure the whole team is strictly on the same page.

items.title: Technical Director & Admin Guide
items.text:
Welcome to the infrastructure core of OpenStudio Hub. This section is dedicated to Technical Directors (TDs), IT administrators, and Production Managers who need to deploy, maintain, and oversee the studio's technical pipeline.

While artists enjoy a seamless, one-click interface, the backend relies on robust networking and version control orchestration.

Navigate through the administrative documentation:

  • B2B Studio Deployment & Provisioning: A comprehensive guide to packaging the global configuration into .seed files for zero-friction Day 0 deployments.
  • VCS Abstraction (SVN / Git LFS): Technical details on how the Hub abstractly supports both SVN and Git LFS under the hood.
  • Process Guardian & Corruption Prevention: Understand how the Hub protects your repository by preventing orphan server locks and safely handling crash recoveries.

items.title: Artist Survival Guide
items.text:
Welcome to your new workspace! The OpenStudio Hub was designed with one simple philosophy: Artists should only focus on art.

You no longer need to worry about naming conventions, folder structures, or configuring add-ons. The Hub handles all the technical heavy lifting, Version Control System (VCS) commands, and server connections automatically.

Follow this guide to master your daily workflow:

  • Getting Started: Learn how to log in, understand your dashboard, and see how the Hub securely manages your credentials in RAM (Zero-Disk Passwords).
  • The Daily Workflow: A simple, step-by-step guide on how to use the "Work" and "Publish" buttons to launch your pre-configured Blender environment and submit your tasks for review.
  • Managing Feedback & Notes: Learn how to read supervisor correction notes and mark them as acknowledged directly inside the Hub's Activity Feed, without ever opening your web browser.

items.title: Features Overview
items.text:
OpenStudio Hub is built around solving daily frustrations for artists and studios by eliminating technical friction. This section explores the core tools designed to automate your pipeline, protect your intellectual property, and remove human error from the equation.

Explore our key features:

  • Automated QA & Auto-Fixing: Learn how the Gatekeeper engine detects and automatically fixes missing textures, dirty geometry, and incorrect naming conventions before an artist can publish their work.
  • Vendor Jailing & Sparse Checkout: Discover how the system isolates projects so external freelancers (vendors) only download the specific files they need, saving bandwidth and protecting your IP.
  • Automated Task Orchestration: See how direct Kitsu integration translates database tasks into physical folder paths and creates master .blend files automatically.
  • Standardized Workspaces & Sandboxing: Understand how the Hub ensures the entire team uses the exact same Blender version and tools by running them in an isolated environment.

items.title: B2B Studio Deployment & Provisioning
items.text: Deploying a pipeline tool across a studio of 50+ artists can be a logistical nightmare. OpenStudio Hub simplifies Day 0 deployment by centralizing the entire studio infrastructure into a single configuration state.

items.title: The Global Configuration
items.text:
The core of the Hub's behavior is driven by a master settings.json file. This file acts as the single source of truth for the studio, defining variables such as: * Nextcloud/NAS Root Paths. * Kitsu API URLs. * VCS Engine topology (SVN vs. Git). * Cloud Services and AI Telemetry activation.

The Hub is OS-agnostic: it dynamically detects the host operating system (Windows, Linux, Darwin) to resolve the correct local workspace root automatically.

items.title: Day 0 Provisioning (The .seed File)
items.text: To provision multiple workstations without manually configuring paths on each machine, the Hub utilizes a Studio Seed Generator. * The system packages and obfuscates the global configuration into a .seed file. * This file is compressed using zlib and base64 for secure and seamless injection into other workstations. * On Day 0, a new artist simply clicks "Load Studio Seed" on the login screen, selects the .seed file, and their Hub is instantly connected to the studio's specific database, network drives, and VCS backend.

items.title: Process Guardian & Corruption Prevention
items.text: Data corruption and stuck server locks are among the most frustrating issues for Technical Directors to resolve. OpenStudio Hub acts as a strict Process Guardian to ensure the repository remains healthy, even during abrupt system failures.

items.title: Lock Prevention & Application Sandboxing
items.text: When an artist opens a file, the Hub claims a lock on the Version Control Server to prevent other artists from overwriting the work. * If the artist attempts to close the OpenStudio Hub while their 3D application is still running, the Hub blocks its own closure. * This strict behavior prevents version control locks from remaining stuck on the server, which would otherwise freeze production for that specific asset.

items.title: Crash Recovery Policy
items.text: Power outages and forced shutdowns happen. To handle these scenarios, the Hub features an automated recovery policy: * Pre-Flight Cleanup: Before launching a new session, the Hub's thread executes a cleanup() method to sanitize the local workspace. * Local Lock Resolution: If the system detects that a file is locked, but the lock belongs to the current active user from a previously crashed session, the Hub ignores the error, declares a "Recovered Session," and safely launches the software.

items.title: VCS Abstraction (SVN / Git LFS)
items.text:
Modern studios have diverse infrastructure needs. Some rely on the centralized locking mechanisms of Apache Subversion (SVN), while others prefer the distributed nature of Git coupled with Git LFS.

OpenStudio Hub solves this through a robust architectural pattern: VCS Abstraction.

items.title: How the Abstraction Layer Works
items.text:
The Hub does not hardcode version control commands into its application logic. Instead, it relies on an AbstractVCS interface that defines base methods such as sparse_pull(), commit(), and lock().

  • The VCS Router: When the application boots, a VCSRouter reads the studio's configuration and dynamically instantiates the correct concrete adapter (e.g., SVNAdapter or GitLFSAdapter).
  • Seamless Polymorphism: The Hub is capable of supporting SVN or Git LFS under the exact same abstract interface.
  • Artist Transparency: For the end-user (the artist), this underlying complexity is completely invisible. They simply interact with the "Work" and "Publish" buttons, while the VCSRouter dispatches the correct network commands in the background.

items.title: Serialized Binary Access (Needs-Lock)
items.text: To prevent simultaneous file corruption on binary files (like .blend), the concrete adapters enforce strict file locking. The VCS adapter will execute svn lock before launching the DCC, and intercept the closure of the environment to mandate an svn unlock, safely passing the baton to the rest of the team.

items.title: The Daily Workflow: Work & Publish
items.text: OpenStudio Hub simplifies your daily routine into two main actions: clicking Work to start, and clicking Publish when you are ready for review.

items.title: 1. Starting your Task (The "Work" Button)
items.text: When you find your assigned task on the dashboard, simply click the Work button. * What happens? The Hub automatically launches your isolated Blender environment and opens your .blend file. * Dynamic Creation: If the file doesn't exist yet, the Hub's Shot Builder dynamically generates it from the studio template so you don't start with an empty canvas. * Context Injection: The interface is pre-navigated to your specific task context, and only the tools you need (like the Flamenco Render Farm for lighting artists) are enabled.

items.title: 2. Working & Telemetry
items.text: While you work, the Hub operates silently in the background: * Auto-Save: The system enforces an automatic save of your .blend file every 30 minutes. * Idle Tracking: An idle tracker pauses your time logging if you step away from your workstation for more than 5 minutes, ensuring your timesheets are perfectly accurate.

items.title: 3. Submitting your Work (The "Push / Publish" Button)
items.text: When your task is ready for review, hit Publish. Before the file is uploaded, the Gatekeeper audits your scene. * Silent Cleanup: It automatically purges orphan data and ignores temporary collections (like __TEMP__). * The Concierge Pop-up: If you accidentally linked a texture or HDRI from your personal Downloads folder, the Hub will intercept the publish and show a pop-up. It will ask you to classify the file, and then it will automatically copy it to the correct server folder and fix the paths for you. * Scale Auto-Fix: If any of your meshes have unapplied rotations or scales, the Gatekeeper will apply them automatically to prevent broken rigs down the line.

items.title: Managing Feedback & Notes
items.text: Review cycles and supervisor feedback are an essential part of production. OpenStudio Hub brings this communication directly to your desktop, keeping you in the zone.

items.title: The Integrated Activity Feed
items.text:
Instead of constantly switching between Blender and your web browser to check Kitsu for updates, you can manage your feedback directly inside the Hub.

  • Centralized Inbox: The Hub features an integrated Activity Feed that displays all notes, retakes, and approvals assigned to your tasks.
  • Acknowledge Notes: When you read a correction note from your supervisor, you can mark it as read by using the "Acknowledge" action directly from the Hub's interface. This instantly syncs with the Kitsu database, letting your supervisor know you have seen the feedback.

By keeping communication inside the Hub, you minimize distractions and maintain a seamless, focused workflow from your first draft to the final approved shot.

items.title: Getting Started
items.text: Welcome to OpenStudio Hub! This guide will help you set up your workspace and understand your new dashboard. Our goal is to let you focus entirely on your art, while the Hub handles the folders, files, and server connections behind the scenes.

items.title: 1. Logging In
items.text: Launch the OpenStudio Hub application. You will be greeted by the login screen. * Enter your studio credentials (the same ones you use for Kitsu/Gazu). * Security Note: The Hub uses a "Zero-Disk Password" policy. This means your version control (SVN) credentials are never saved to your hard drive. You may occasionally see a Just-In-Time (JIT) pop-up asking for your SVN password before downloading files; this is kept securely in your computer's RAM only while the app is open.

items.title: 2. The Artist Dashboard
items.text: Once logged in, you will see your main dashboard (ViewArtist). * Your Tasks: The Hub connects directly to the Kitsu API to display all your assigned tasks (e.g., "TODO", "WIP") as visual cards, complete with status tags and thumbnails. * Dynamic Syncing: If your supervisor assigns you a new task while the Hub is open, you don't need to restart the app. Simply click the "↻ Reload" button at the top of your panel to fetch the latest assignments.

items.title: 3. Your Workspace
items.text: You don't need to configure Blender, install add-ons, or map network drives. The Hub downloads the studio-approved Blender version and sets up a standard, isolated workspace for you automatically.

items.title: Automated QA & Auto-Fixing (Gatekeeper)
items.text:
In a fast-paced production environment, sending a file back and forth between artists and supervisors due to technical errors—like an unapplied scale or a missing texture—is a massive waste of time and money.

OpenStudio Hub solves this natively through its Gatekeeper engine.

items.title: What is the Gatekeeper?
items.text:
The Gatekeeper is a strict, automated Quality Assurance (QA) protocol that runs silently in the background. Before an artist is allowed to push or publish their work to the server, the Gatekeeper audits the scene to ensure it complies with the studio's technical standards.

Instead of just warning the user, it actively attempts to fix the issues for them.

items.title: 1. Out-of-Bounds Dependency Resolution
items.text: A classic mistake: an artist links a texture or an HDRI from their personal Downloads folder instead of the project's network drive (NAS). * Detection: The Gatekeeper scans all external dependency paths in Blender. * Auto-Fix (The Concierge): If a file resides outside the OPENSTUDIO_PROJECT_ROOT, it triggers an interactive pop-up. The artist classifies the file, and the Hub automatically copies the asset to the correct shared folder and makes the paths relative. No more "pink meshes".

items.title: 2. Geometry Sanity & Scale Auto-Fix
items.text: Delivering an asset with unapplied rotations or incorrect scales will break rigs and downstream simulations. * Detection: Scans all published objects for Scale anomalies (anything != 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) and unapplied rotations. * Auto-Fix: Automatically applies transformations (bpy.ops.object.transform_apply) and enforces the studio's strict naming conventions (e.g., {asset_name}-{suffix}).

items.title: 3. Silent Orphan Purging
items.text: To keep files lightweight and repository sizes small, the system runs a transparent purge of unused data blocks (orphan data) and explicitly excludes temporary collections (like __TEMP__) from the final publish.

items.title: Automated Task Orchestration
items.text: Human error in folder naming and directory structures is the silent killer of 3D pipelines. OpenStudio Hub completely removes the artist and the manager from the file-creation equation by integrating seamlessly with Kitsu / Gazu API.

items.title: 1. Batch Task Spawning
items.text: Production Managers (PMs) no longer need to manually set up project folders. Through the Hub's interface, a PM can select approved storyboards or edit master shots, and the system will automatically trigger a Batch Task Spawning routine. The Hub generates the entire task tree (Animation, Rigging, Layout) and injects the master .blend templates directly into the SVN repository in one click.

items.title: 2. The Path Resolver Engine
items.text: Artists never have to worry about where to save their files. The Hub's internal PathResolver translates the Kitsu Task API data into absolute physical paths on the disk. It automatically evaluates if the task belongs to a Shot or an Asset, routing it to the correct standardized template (e.g., shots/{seq}/{shot}/).

items.title: 3. One-Click Context Injection
items.text: When an artist clicks "Work" on their Hub dashboard, the magic happens under the hood: * The system injects Kitsu IDs (Task ID, Entity ID, Sequence ID) directly into Blender's RAM (Scene RNA). * The artist's 3D interface is pre-navigated to their specific task context. * The UI workspace is forced into the correct layout (e.g., forcing the Video Sequence Editor for editorial tasks or 2D Animation for Storyboards) based on the assigned discipline.

items.title: Standardized Workspaces & Sandboxing
items.text:
"It works on my machine" is a phrase that should never be heard in a professional pipeline. Mismatched software versions, outdated add-ons, and customized user preferences cause catastrophic render failures and broken files.

OpenStudio Hub enforces a strict Golden Path through zero-configuration Sandboxing.

items.title: 1. Pristine DCC Deployment
items.text: The Hub acts as an autonomous package manager. It asynchronously scrapes and downloads the exact, studio-approved Blender executable directly from download.blender.org. The software is extracted into an isolated local vault (e.g., 06_conf_LOCAL), completely ignoring any pre-existing Blender installations on the artist's machine.

items.title: 2. Environment Variable Injection
items.text: To guarantee that the entire team uses the exact same tools without conflicts, the Hub launches Blender using injected environment variables like BLENDER_USER_RESOURCES. This forces the software to read configurations and add-ons strictly from the controlled Hub ecosystem.

items.title: 3. Dynamic Tooling & Add-on Sync
items.text: Before the software even launches, the Hub performs a silent sync. * It pulls the latest studio tools (like the Kitsu add-on and Asset Pipeline) from the central NAS. * It forces physical studio preferences (like injecting the OPENSTUDIO_PROJECT_ROOT path into the add-on settings), instantly reverting any manual, unauthorized modifications made by the user. * Features are context-aware: Tools like the Flamenco Render Farm submitter are dynamically hidden from modelers and automatically enabled only for lighting and rendering artists.

items.title: Vendor Jailing & Sparse Checkout
items.text:
When collaborating with external freelancers (Vendors), studios face two critical bottlenecks: Intellectual Property (IP) Security and Bandwidth Waste. Forcing a remote animator to download a 500GB repository just to work on a single shot is highly inefficient and exposes your entire production data.

OpenStudio Hub introduces a Zero-Trust architecture through its Vendor Jailing engine.

items.title: How It Solves the Problem
items.text: Instead of performing a full repository clone, the Hub evaluates the user's role upon login. If the artist is tagged as a vendor, the system automatically shifts to a highly restrictive Sparse Checkout mode.

items.title: 1. Granular Downloads via Manifests
items.text: The system downloads only the specific task folder assigned to the artist. To ensure the 3D scene doesn't break, the Hub scans a local dependency manifest (*-meta.json) generated by the DCC. It then executes a recursive algorithm to fetch exclusively the exact textures, caches, and linked assets required for that specific shot.

items.title: 2. Relative Path Translation
items.text: To avoid broken links without downloading massive parent folders, the Hub translates native Blender relative paths (//) into absolute Version Control System (VCS) paths. This guarantees zero broken links for the artist without saturating the production database.

items.title: 3. Automated Workspace Purging
items.text: As a vendor finishes a task and moves to a new one, the Hub automatically purges the old, approved shots from their local hard drive. This prevents progressive IP leakage and keeps the freelancer's workstation lightweight and focused.
